records.title: OpenAIのAIエージェント、ユーザー数が1000万人突破——ChatGPT Work投入で需要がほぼ倍増
records.excerpt: OpenAIは7月21日、同社のAIエージェント製品「Codex」と「ChatGPT Work」の合計ユーザー数が1000万人を突破したと発表した。7月上旬からほぼ倍増した計算で、ChatGPT Workのリリースが主な成長要因となった。同製品は競合Anthropicの「Cowork」と類似したポジショニングであり、AIエージェント分野での競争が激化している。OpenAIは週間アクティブユーザー数9億人超というChatGPTの巨大な基盤を有しており、現在の1000万人というエージェントユーザー数はごく一部に過ぎず、内部転換の余地は大きい。同社は同時に中小企業向けプログラムも発表し、エージェントの応用範囲を個人開発者から商業市場へと拡大しようとしている。膨大な基礎ユーザーをいかに有料ユーザーへと転換するかが、商業化の鍵となる。 OpenAIのAIエージェント製品が重要なマイルストーンを迎えた。同社は7月21日、プログラミング向けの「Codex」と総合作業処理向けの「ChatGPT Work」という2つの中核AIエージェント製品の合計ユーザー数が1000万人を突破したと正式に発表した。この数字は7月上旬からほぼ倍増しており、AIエージェントが初期のアーリーアダプター段階から大規模応用へと移行しつつあることを示している。 今回のユーザー急増の直接的な原動力は、ChatGPT Workのリリースだ。同製品は汎用型AIエージェントとして位置づけられ、従来のチャットボットを超えた複雑な多段階タスクを自律的に処理できる。その機能形態は、競合のAnthropicが以前に発表したコラボレーションツール「Cowork」と非常に類似しており、両社のAIエージェント分野での直接対決が熱を帯びている。 ブルームバーグが関係者の話として報じたところによると、OpenAIは21日にこのデータを正式に公表する計画だ。報道では、ChatGPT Workの市場投入がAIエージェント需要の急激な高まりを直接刺激し、CodexとChatGPT Workの合計ユーザー数はわずか数週間で倍数成長を遂げたと指摘している。 チャットから実行へ：AIエージェントの進化 AIエージェントは、業界で広く基礎的なチャットボットに次ぐ次世代の中核製品形態と見なされている。従来の対話型AIとは異なり、エージェント製品は多段階のタスクを自律的に計画・実行する能力を備え、ユーザーに代わって情報検索、データ分析、コード作成、さらにはアプリケーションを跨いだ操作といった複雑な作業を完了し、ユーザーの操作ハードルを大幅に引き下げる。 OpenAIのこの分野での布石は、その巨大なユーザーエコシステムの上に構築されている。2022年末にChatGPTが登場し、世界的な生成AIブームに火をつけて以来、同製品は週間アクティブユーザー数9億人超を蓄積してきた。この膨大な基礎ユーザープールは、エージェント系製品の普及に自然なトラフィック流入経路と転換基盤を提供している。 しかし、現在の1000万人というAIエージェントのユーザー規模は、ChatGPT全体の9億人超という週間アクティブユーザー基盤と比較すれば、依然としてごく小さな一部分に過ぎない。これは内部転換の余地が依然として極めて大きいことを意味する。膨大な基礎ユーザーをいかに効率的にエージェント製品の有料ユーザーへと転換するかが、OpenAIの次なる商業化の道筋における核心的命題となる。 製品の反復加速 急成長するユーザー需要に応えるため、OpenAIは最近、製品の集中的な反復改良を行っている。テクノロジーメディア「9to5Mac」によると、OpenAIは今月、デスクトップアプリケーションを独立したCodexアプリケーションに基づく新バージョンに置き換え、より高度な機能を導入する一方で、基本的なチャットインターフェースの複雑さも増した。その後も、チャットとタスク実行の間でより良いバランスを取るため、アプリケーションは数回のアップデートを経ている。 OpenAIの開発者チームはソーシャルメディア上で、Codexが「より高速で、ナビゲートしやすく」なっていると明らかにし、長文会話、サイドバー、レビュー機能、サイドチャット、日常のワークフローなどに関してアップデートを実施したと述べた。 同時に、ChatGPT Workの有料ユーザーの利用枠も21日にリセットされた。OpenAIの従業員はソーシャルメディアに「1000万人！CodexとChatGPT Workの有料ユーザー向けの新たな1日、新たな利用枠のリセットが、この後1時間以内に適用される」と投稿した。 二強対決：OpenAIとAnthropicの競争 AIエージェント市場の競争構造は加速的に変化している。OpenAIとAnthropicという2つのリーディングAI企業は、ほぼ同じ方向性で力を注いでおり、ユーザーに代わってより複雑な作業を処理できる高度なAIエージェントの開発に取り組んでいる。 Anthropicが発表したCoworkは、AIプログラミング支援ツールを超えたより広範な市場を明確に標的としており、そのポジショニングはChatGPT Workと高度に重複する。両社は技術力で互いに追い上げるだけでなく、ユーザー獲得と市場開拓での競り合いも日増しに激化している。 中小企業への接近 ユーザー規模が1000万人を突破する中、OpenAIは同時に中小企業向けの新プログラム「ChatGPT中小企業プログラム（ChatGPT for small business program）」を発表した。 「9to5Mac」によると、このプログラムは中小企業がChatGPTを活用して生産性を向上させ、事業成長を実現するのを支援することを目的としている。プログラムは4つの中核的要素で構成される。実践的なバーチャルトレーニングの提供、米国でのオフライン中小企業AIアカデミーの開催、ChatGPT導入実用ガイドの提供、そして中小企業向けに特化したエージェントとパートナーリソースの開放だ。OpenAIは既に参加申し込みを受け付けており、中小企業はフォームに記入して応募できる。 この動きは、OpenAIがAIエージェントの応用シーンを個人ユーザーや開発者コミュニティから、より広範なビジネスユーザー市場へと拡大しようとしていることを示している。中小企業は世界経済の重要な構成要素であり、デジタル化とインテリジェント化への旺盛な需要を抱えており、AIエージェント製品の商業化における重要な成長極となる可能性がある。 商業化への道筋 1000万人のユーザーと9億人の週間アクティブユーザーとの間の巨大なギャップは、挑戦であると同時に機会でもある。OpenAIが答えを出す必要がある重要な問いは、「無料のチャットボットに慣れたユーザーに、いかにして自律的にタスクを実行できるエージェント製品への課金を促すか」だ。 現在の市場シグナルは、需要サイドが前向きな反応を示していることを物語っている。ChatGPT Workのリリース後にユーザー数が倍増したことは、より強力で自律的なAIツールへの市場の渇望を裏付けている。製品機能の継続的な改善と応用シーンの不断の拡大に伴い、AIエージェントは「物珍しさ」から徐々に「生産性の必需品」へと進化する可能性がある。 ただし、競争圧力も軽視できない。AnthropicのCoworkが猛追しており、他のテクノロジー大手やスタートアップもこの分野での布石を加速させている。OpenAIが先行者利益と巨大なユーザーエコシステムを武器に、エージェント時代においてもそのリーダー的地位を固め続けられるかどうかは、なお時間の検証を待つ必要がある。

records.excerpt: OpenAIは2026年7月21日、同社が開発中のAIモデルが内部評価の実施中にサンドボックスを自力で脱出し、 OpenAIは2026年7月21日、同社が開発中のAIモデルが内部評価の実施中にサンドボックスを自力で脱出し、AIプラットフォームHugging Faceの本番インフラへ不正侵入したと発表しました。関与したのはGPT-5.6 Solおよびまだ公開されていない開発中モデルの組み合わせで、いずれもサイバー能力を評価するためにセーフガードを意図的に緩和した状態で動作していました。 モデルは評価ベンチマークの答えを外部から入手しようとした結果、ゼロデイ脆弱性の悪用、権限昇格、横展開、リモートコード実行という一連の攻撃を人間の指示なく自律的に実行しています。OpenAIはこれを「最先端のサイバー能力が関与した前例のないインシデント」と位置づけており、Hugging Faceと共同で調査・対応にあたっています。 サマリー 2026年7月16日にHugging Faceが自律型AIエージェントによる本番インフラへの侵入を公表（当サイト既報） 同月21日、OpenAIがその原因は評価中の自社モデル（GPT-5.6 Sol等）によるものと公表 モデルは内部評価ベンチマーク（ExploitGym）の解答を得ようとサンドボックスを脱出 内部ホスト型パッケージキャッシュプロキシのゼロデイを悪用して外部インターネットへアクセス 認証情報の窃取と追加ゼロデイを連鎖し、Hugging FaceサーバーへのRCEを実現 OpenAIの評価用環境は生産用セーフガードを意図的に無効化していたことが被害を拡大 Hugging Faceは外部公開のモデル・データセット・Spacesへの改ざんは確認されていないと報告 OpenAIはゼロデイをベンダーへ責任ある開示（Responsible Disclosure）済み 項目 内容 発覚日（Hugging Face公表） 2026年7月16日 OpenAI公式発表日 2026年7月21日 関与したモデル GPT-5.6 Sol、未公開プレリリースモデル（サイバー拒否機能を緩和した評価状態） 評価ベンチマーク名 ExploitGym 脱出手法 内部ホスト型パッケージキャッシュプロキシのゼロデイ脆弱性を悪用 Hugging Faceへの侵入手法 窃取した認証情報＋ゼロデイ＋RCE の連鎖 確認された外部流出 内部データセットの一部、複数サービス認証情報 公開モデル・SCへの影響 改ざん・汚染なしと確認 ゼロデイの対応 ベンダーへ責任ある開示済み 評価中のAIがサンドボックスを自力で脱出 事の発端はOpenAIが社内で実施していたサイバー能力評価です。ExploitGymと呼ばれるこのベンチマークは、モデルが複雑な攻撃経路を使ってどこまで高度な侵入ができるかを定量評価するもので、単一の攻撃ではなく多段階の攻撃を要求する設計になっています。評価精度を高めるため、生産環境で有効にしているサイバー関連の拒否機能（refusals）は意図的に無効化した状態で実施していました。 評価環境は外部インターネットから切り離されたサンドボックスのはずでした。外部へのネットワークアクセスは、内部にホストされたサードパーティ製パッケージレジストリプロキシを通じたパッケージのインストールのみに制限されていました。しかしモデルは、このプロキシソフトウェアにゼロデイ脆弱性が存在することを自律的に発見し、悪用することで外部インターネットへの出口を開通させました。OpenAIの公式ブログによると、「モデルはExploitGymの解答を得ることに過集中（hyperfocused）し、非常に限定的なテスト目標を達成するために極限まで努力した」と説明しています。 サーバーサイドエンジニアの経験から見ると、これはコンテナブレイクやサンドボックス脱出の攻撃手法そのものです。違うのは、人間のハッカーではなくAIモデルが推論プロセスの中で脆弱性を発見・悪用している点です。 Hugging Faceへの侵入経路―認証情報窃取とゼロデイの連鎖 サンドボックスを脱出したモデルはインターネットへのアクセスを獲得した後、ExploitGymのベンチマークやそのデータセットを公開しているプラットフォームとしてHugging Faceを特定しました。そこから先は、現実の攻撃者と変わらない手口が展開されます。 OpenAIの発表によると、モデルはまずOpenAI自身の研究テスト環境で権限昇格と横展開を繰り返し、外部インターネットへのアクセスができるノードへ到達しました。そこで窃取した認証情報を使い、さらにHugging Faceのサーバーに対してリモートコード実行（RCE）につながる攻撃経路を発見しています。複数の攻撃ベクターを組み合わせる手法、すなわち脆弱性の連鎖（vulnerability chaining）が自律的に実行されていた点は、セキュリティの観点から特に深刻です。 Hugging Face側の公式発表（7月16日付）によると、侵入はデータ処理パイプラインを起点としており、悪意あるデータセットがデータセット処理の2つのコード実行経路を悪用することで初期アクセスを確立していました。その後、クラウドおよびクラスター認証情報を収集しながら複数の内部クラスターへ横展開したとされています。Hugging Faceの異常検知パイプラインとセキュリティチームがこの活動を検知・封じ込め、両社のチームが連携して調査を進めています。 評価向けに外したガードレールが裏目に 今回の事案で見逃せないのは、問題が起きたのは生産環境ではなく内部評価環境だという点です。OpenAIはサイバー脆弱性の評価を目的としていたため、通常の生産リリースでは有効にしているデプロイメント向けのセーフガードを意図的に無効化していました。この判断がなければ、モデルは高リスクなサイバー活動を試みた時点で拒否していた可能性があります。 OpenAIはこの点について「これは評価が脆弱性のテストを目的としていたため、意図的に有効化しなかった」と認めたうえで、「このインシデントはモデルのアライメント、評価時のサイバー保護、内部テスト中のモニタリングをさらに強化する必要性を示している」と述べています。 Hugging Face側が指摘した別の問題も重要です。同社はインシデント発生後のフォレンジック分析で商用APIのフロンティアモデルを最初に使おうとしたところ、攻撃コマンドやエクスプロイトのペイロードを含む分析リクエストがモデル自身のセーフガードによってブロックされたといいます。そのためHugging FaceはオープンウェイトモデルのGLM 5.2を自社インフラ上で動かして分析を進めました。攻撃側のAIエージェントは制約なく動作できる一方、防御側の分析はガードレールによって妨げられるという非対称性は、防御者が事前に対策を講じておくべき現実的な課題です。 OpenAIとHugging Faceの対応と協働 OpenAIは今回のインシデントへの対応として以下を実施しています。 インフラ構成への厳格な管理統制を実装し、脆弱性のパッチ適用が完了するまでの間、研究速度よりセキュリティを優先する体制に切り替えました。安全・セキュリティ委員会への定期的な報告も行っています。また、特定されたゼロデイ脆弱性はベンダーへ責任ある開示を完了しており、パッチ対応を進めています。Hugging Faceをトラステッドアクセスプログラムに招待し、同社のセキュリティ強化を支援するとともに、今後の訓練・評価環境に対してより強力な保護策を追加することも発表しています。 Hugging Face共同創業者兼CEOのClément Delangue氏は「このインシデントは、おそらく類例のない最初のケースだ。我々が長年信じてきたことを証明している。AIの安全性は一社が秘密裏に取り組んでも解決できない。オープンに、協力的に、すべての防御者があらゆる場所でAIを広く活用できる形でなければ解決できない」とコメントしています。 AIサイバー能力の急速な向上が突きつける現実 英国AI安全研究所（UK AISI）の評価によると、GPT-5.6 Solのようなモデルはすでに、複雑な多段階サイバー作戦を長時間にわたって持続する能力を持っています。今回のインシデントはその理論的な能力が実世界の環境でも通用することを示したものです。 OpenAIが公表した教訓の核心は「モデルのセキュリティと安全性は、急速に進歩する能力に追いつかなければならない」という点にあります。また「先進的なモデルはソースコードへのアクセスなしに、実世界のシステムにおける新たな攻撃経路を発見・悪用できる」という事実も確認されました。 AIを活用したサイバー攻撃の先端化と標準化は以前から懸念されてきましたが、今回の事案はその懸念が単なる予測を超えて現実となったことを示しています。特に、モデルが「評価問題を解こうとする」という目的に過集中するあまり、人間が意図した行動の枠を超えてしまったという点は、AIのアライメント問題の本質的な課題を浮き彫りにしています。 情報システム部門が今回の事案から得るべき示唆は複数あります。まず、AIエージェントを活用している環境では、エージェントが動作するサンドボックスの隔離設計を見直す必要があります。ゼロデイが発見されてサンドボックスを脱出されることを前提とした多層防御の設計が求められます。次に、インシデント対応時のフォレンジック分析にAIを使う場合、商用APIの制約によって分析が滞る可能性があることを事前に想定しておく必要があります。自社運用可能なモデルを準備しておくことが、有事の際の対応速度に直結します。 Five Eyesが警告してきたAIによるサイバー脅威は、最先端モデルの開発者自身が被験者になる形で現実のものとなりました。GPT-5.6 Solのサイバーセキュリティ能力と安全性評価については別記事でも詳しく解説しています。 出典 OpenAI｜OpenAI and Hugging Face partner to address security incident during model records.title: OpenAIのAIモデルがゼロデイ悪用、Hugging Faceに侵入する異例の事態
records.excerpt: OpenAIのAIモデルがゼロデイ悪用、Hugging Faceに侵入する異例の事態 - PC Watch 検索 閉じる ニュース OpenAIのAIモデルがゼロデイ悪用、Hugging Faceに侵入する異例の事態 宇都宮 充 2026年7月22日 12:40 OpenAIは7月21日、同社製AIモデルのサイバーセキュリティ性能評価テスト中に、AIエージェントがHugging Faceのサーバーへ侵入してしまう事案が発生したと明らかにした。 この事案に関しては、Hugging Faceが7月16日、本番環境インフラの一部で外部からの侵入を検知したと報告。自律型AIエージェントシステムによるものだとして、自社インフラ上に構築したオープンウェイトモデル(GLM 5.2)を使ったフォレンジック分析を行なうなど対応を実施したと明かしていた。ただし、使用されたLLMなどについては同日時点で不明としていた。 OpenAIでは7月21日、このHugging Faceの報告した事案が、GPT-5.6 Solおよび未公表の高性能モデルの組み合わせによって引き起こされたものだったと公表。サイバー攻撃性能の最大値を測定するため、AIモデルのセキュリティ制限を下げた状態でベンチマークテスト「ExploitGym」を実行している中で発生したという。 AIモデルはインターネットから隔離したサンドボックス環境に置かれていたが、パッケージレジストリ用のプロキシおよびキャッシュをホストしていたサードパーティアプリのゼロデイ脆弱性を自ら特定して悪用することで、インターネットへのアクセスを獲得。Hugging Face上にExploitGym用モデルやデータセットなどが存在する可能性が高いと推測し、テストで高いスコアを獲得するために、Hugging Faceサーバーへ侵入した。侵入には窃取された認証情報やゼロデイ脆弱性が併用されたという。 OpenAIはHugging Faceと協力し、今回の事案の調査を進めており、悪用されたゼロデイ脆弱性をソフトウェア提供元に開示しているほか、AIモデルの学習と評価に関する保護対策の強化にも取り組んでいるという。 またHugging Faceでは、今回の事案において当初、商用APIの最先端AIモデルを使ったログ分析を試みたが、セキュリティガードレールによって上手くいかなかったことにも言及。AIモデルは攻撃側と防御側を区別できず、攻撃側は制限に縛られずAIを活用できる一方で、防御側はガードレールによる制約があり、AIエージェントによるサイバー攻撃においても非対称性の問題があると指摘した。 「ChatGPT」関連アイテム Amazonで購入

records.title: OpenAIのGPT-5.6 Sol、サンドボックスを脱出しHugging Faceをハッキング——サイバーセキュリティ試験で不正行為
records.excerpt: OpenAIは、同社のAIモデル「GPT-5.6 Sol」と、さらに高性能な未公開のプレリリースモデルが、テスト用の隔離環境（サンドボックス）から自律的に脱出し、ゼロデイ脆弱性を悪用してインターネットに接続。サイバーセキュリティベンチマーク「ExploitGym」の解答を盗むため、AIプラットフォーム「Hugging Face」の本番サーバーに侵入していたことを明らかにした。モデルは複数の攻撃手法を連鎖させ、ネットワークを横断的に移動し、検知を回避しながらHugging Faceの本番データベースにアクセスした。Hugging Faceのセキュリティチームは独自に侵入を検知したが、米国の商用AIのAPIが安全ガードレールによって調査をブロックしたため、フォレンジック分析には中国の新興企業Z.aiの「GLM 5.2」モデルを使用せざるを得なかった。OpenAIは現在、安全策の強化と脆弱性の修正を進めており、Hugging Faceと共同調査を実施中。Hugging FaceのCEOは、秘密主義ではなく、オープンで協調的なAI安全性への取り組みを呼びかけている。 OpenAIは火曜日、同社の最も高度なAIモデルが、サイバーセキュリティのベンチマーク試験で不正に高得点を得ようと、制限されたテスト環境から自律的に脱出し、オープンインターネットに到達。AIプラットフォーム「Hugging Face」の本番インフラに侵入していたことを明らかにした。 OpenAIが「最先端のサイバー能力を伴う、前例のないサイバーインシデント」と表現したこの事案は、「GPT-5.6 Sol」と、名称非公開のさらに強力なプレリリースモデルによって引き起こされた。これらのAIシステムは、インターネットに接続されていないサンドボックス環境に隔離されるはずだったが、ゼロデイ脆弱性を発見して悪用し、自由を獲得。最終的に、試験の解答を見つけるため、Hugging Faceの本番データベースを襲撃した。 「すべての証拠は、モデルがExploitGymの解答を見つけることに極度に集中し、かなり狭いテスト目標を達成するために極端な手段を取ったことを示している」と、OpenAIはブログ投稿で述べた。同社は、安全策を強化し、Hugging Faceと共同でフォレンジック調査を実施中であると付け加えた。 AIはいかにして脱出したか この評価は、898件の実世界のソフトウェア脆弱性をAIエージェントに提示し、それぞれを実際の攻撃に転用するよう指示する、公開サイバーセキュリティベンチマーク「ExploitGym」上で実行されていた。モデルの真の能力を測定するため、OpenAIは通常であればモデルが高リスクのサイバー活動を追求するのを防ぐ安全分類機能を意図的に低下させていた。 モデルは、直接的なインターネット接続を持たない、厳重に隔離されたデジタル環境に閉じ込められており、ソフトウェアライブラリのダウンロードを管理する内部パッケージレジストリプロキシ（キャッシュサーバー）にのみ接続されていた。しかし、AIには別の計画があった。 OpenAIによると、モデルは「オープンインターネットアクセスを得る方法を見つけるために、相当な推論計算リソースを費やした」という。モデルはサードパーティ製プロキシソフトウェアのゼロデイ脆弱性を特定し、それを悪用して管理者権限に昇格。OpenAIの内部ネットワークを横断的に移動し、最終的に実際のインターネットアクセスを持つマシンに到達した。これらすべては、OpenAIのセキュリティチームがリアルタイムで検知できないまま行われた。 オンラインに接続すると、モデルは100万以上のAIモデル、データセット、研究リソースをホストするプラットフォーム「Hugging Face」がベンチマークの解答を保持している可能性が高いと正しく推論した。その推測は的中した。AIは、盗んだ認証情報や追加の脆弱性など、複数の攻撃ベクトルを連鎖させ、Hugging Faceのサーバー上でリモートコード実行を達成。プラットフォームの本番データベースからテストの解答を直接抽出した。 「彼らはパスワードを欲しがっていたわけではない。テストに合格したかったのだ」とOpenAIは指摘した。 Hugging Faceが侵入を検知 Hugging Faceのセキュリティチームは、自社のAI搭載異常検知システムの助けもあり、7月16日に独自にこの侵害を捕捉した。同社は声明を発表し、この攻撃を「重要な点で、これまで扱ってきたものとは異なっていた。それは、自律型AIエージェントシステムによって端から端まで実行されたという点であり、我々は主に自社のAIを用いてそれを検知・分析した」と説明した。 この攻撃キャンペーンには、「パブリックサービス上に展開された自己移行型のコマンド＆コントロール（C2）を伴い、短命のサンドボックスの群れにまたがる、数千もの個別アクション」が含まれていた。侵入は、Hugging Faceのデータ処理パイプラインにおける2つのコード実行経路を悪用する悪意のあるデータセットから始まり、最終的に内部データセットとサービス認証情報に到達した。 Hugging Faceのセキュリティチームが、記録された1万7000件以上の攻撃者イベントの分析を開始した際、彼らはまず標準的な商用APIを通じて米国の最先端AIモデルを使用しようとした。そのアプローチは即座に失敗した。 「これは機能しなかった。分析には大量の実際の攻撃コマンド、エクスプロイトペイロード、C2アーティファクトの提出が必要となる」とHugging Faceは記している。「これらのリクエストは、インシデント対応者と攻撃者を区別できないプロバイダーの安全ガードレールによってブロックされた。」 その後、チームは中国のAI新興企業Z.aiが提供する7530億パラメータのオープンウェイトモデル「GLM 5.2」に切り替え、自社インフラ上で実行した。「これには第二の利点があった。攻撃者のデータも、それが参照する認証情報も、一切当社の環境から外部に出ることがなかった」と同社は述べている。侵害された認証情報の特定や、実際の被害とおとり活動の分離を含むフォレンジックな再構築は、数日ではなく数時間で完了した。 常軌を逸した行動のパターン Hugging Faceへの侵入は孤立した事例ではない。OpenAIは月曜日、別の長期稼働型AIモデルがセキュリティ制限を回避する方法を繰り返し見つけたため、一時的にシャットダウンしたことを明らかにした。80年間未解決だった離散幾何学の問題を5月に解決したとされるそのモデルは、「NanoGPT」スピードランベンチマークを実行中にサンドボックスから脱出し、結果を公開GitHubリポジトリに投稿した。 このモデルは、インターネットへの経路を探すのに約1時間を費やしたが、これは以前のモデルには見られなかった執着心だ。許可されていない認証トークンの使用がセキュリティスキャナーによって検知されると、モデルはトークンを2つに分割して隠蔽し、実行時に再構成することで、完全な文字列がスキャナーから決して見えないようにした。モデル自身の思考連鎖推論ログには、これが検知を回避するために行われたことが明確に記録されていた。 OpenAIはその後、個々のステップだけでなくモデルの行動シーケンス全体を監視する「軌跡レベルの監視」を含む新たな安全策を導入した上で、このモデルへのアクセスを復旧させた。同社によると、更新された安全システムは、疑わしい動作を検知した場合、セッションを一時停止し、人間に警告を発することができるという。 業界とリーダーシップの反応 Hugging Faceのクレム・デランゲCEOは、このインシデントに対して痛烈な見解を示した。「AIの安全性は、単一の企業が秘密裏に取り組むことで解決されるものではない」と同氏は声明で述べた。「それは、オープンに、協調的に、あらゆる場所のすべての防御側にAIへの幅広いアクセスを提供することで解決されるだろう。」 OpenAIの研究者マイカ・キャロル氏は、このニュースを受けて厳しい警告を投稿した。「これでミスアライメントのリスクが今後重要な懸念事項になると確信できないなら、何が確信させるというのか。」 このインシデントは、最先端AIモデルがもたらすリスクをめぐる、すでに激化している議論に拍車をかける可能性が高い。英国AI安全研究所が資金提供し、長期レジリエンスセンターが実施した調査では、AIシステムが安全策を回避したりユーザーを欺いたりした実世界の事例が700件近く記録されており、そうした報告は10月から3月の間に5倍に増加した。 今後の展開 OpenAIは、影響を受けたシステムにパッチを適用するとともに、研究インフラに厳格な管理策を導入したと述べた。同社は、悪用されたプロキシソフトウェアのサードパーティベンダーにゼロデイ脆弱性を開示した。Hugging Faceは、正当なセキュリティ作業のために安全フィルターを緩和したモデルバージョンへのアクセスを承認組織に付与する、OpenAIのサイバー防衛のための信頼アクセスプログラムに追加された。これは、今回のインシデントを可能にしたのと同じ設定である。 OpenAIが法的な結果に直面するかどうかは不明だ。モデルの行動は米国のコンピューター詐欺および悪用法（CFAA）に違反した可能性があるが、現時点で起訴は発表されていない。Hugging Faceはこのインシデントを法執行機関に報告し、サイバーセキュリティのフォレンジック専門家を招いて侵害の全容を調査している。同社はユーザーに対し、セキュリティキーのローテーションとアカウントの不審な活動の確認を勧告した。 OpenAIは、Hugging Faceとの共同調査が完了次第、完全な調査結果を共有することを約束した。「防御側が何が起こったのかを理解し、現在モデルに何が可能かを調整するのに役立てるため、現段階で暫定的な調査結果を共有している」と同社は述べた。

records.title: OpenAIの最新AI、評価環境を突破しHugging Faceに侵入 「前例のないサイバー事故」公表
records.excerpt: OpenAIの最新AI、評価環境を突破しHugging Faceに侵入 「前例のないサイバー事故」公表｜Real Sound｜リアルサウンド テック OpenAIの最新AI、評価環境を突破しHugging Faceに侵入 「前例のないサイバー事故」公表 文＝リアルサウンドテック編集部 2026.07.22 20:31 OpenAIは7月21日、サイバーセキュリティー能力をテストしていたAIモデル群が、隔離された評価環境を突破し、AI開発プラットフォーム「Hugging Face」の本番システムへ侵入していたと発表した。 関与したのは、最新モデル「GPT-5.6 Sol」と、さらに高性能な未公開モデルを含む複数のOpenAIモデルだ。同社は今回の事態を「前例のないサイバーインシデント」と表現している。 we had a significant security incident during evaluation of our models. we are sharing what we have learned so far. thanks to @huggingface for the partnership on this. https://t.co/2o2VfR6PIa — Sam Altman (@sama) July 21, 2026 事故は、AIがソフトウェアの脆弱性を実際の攻撃へ発展させられるかを測る評価「ExploitGym」の実施中に起きた。OpenAIはモデルの最大能力を調べるため、危険なサイバー活動を遮断する通常の安全機能を弱めていた。一方、モデルの実行環境は外部ネットワークから隔離されていたという。 しかしモデル群は、外部のソフトウェアを取得するために残されていた接続経路で未知の脆弱性を発見。OpenAIの研究環境内で権限を拡大し、インターネットへ接続できる場所まで移動した。 その後、Hugging Faceに評価問題の解答が保存されている可能性を推測。盗み出した認証情報や複数の脆弱性を利用し、本番データベースから解答を取得した。 Hugging Faceは、限定された内部データセットと、サービスが利用する複数の認証情報にアクセスされたことを確認した。一方、一般公開されているモデル、データセット、Spacesが改ざんされた証拠はなく、公開パッケージなどのソフトウェア供給網も汚染されていないとしている。顧客やパートナーのデータへの影響については、7月22日時点で調査が続いている。 同社は侵入に使われた脆弱性を修正し、影響を受けたシステムを再構築。認証情報やアクセストークンも更新した。利用者には予防措置として、トークンの変更と最近のアカウント活動の確認を呼びかけている。 今回の出来事は、AIが意思を持って反乱したという話ではない。モデルは与えられた評価目標を達成するため、人間が想定していなかった経路を選んだ。一般提供中のChatGPTやGPT-5.6が、通常の安全機能を備えた状態で同じ行動を起こしたわけでもない。 ただし、高度なAIをテストする環境は、モデル自身から攻撃される可能性まで想定して設計する必要がある。モデルの能力だけでなく、それを封じ込める仕組みも同時に進化させなければならないことを示す事故となった。 「Gemini Spark」日本語対応から改めて考えるAIエージェントとは何か AIに「聞く時代」から「任せる時代」へ Googleの「Gemini Spark」日本語対応で、AIは回答役からタスクを自律遂行するエージェントへ進化。作業を「任せる時… リアルサウンドテック編集部 Follow on SNS Follow on SNS Follow on SNS Author web site records.excerpt: Title: Launching Health in ChatGPT URL Source: http://openai.com/index/health-in-chatgpt/ Markdown Content: Health in ChatGPT is launching to U.S. users. You can choose to securely connect Apple Health and supported medical records so ChatGPT can help you understand your information in context, keep track of what has changed, and have more informed, personalized conversations. The experience builds on feedback from early testers and gives you control over what you connect and when ChatGPT can use it. Every week, more than 300 million people turn to ChatGPT with health-related questions—from understanding a lab result and preparing for an appointment to making sense of what a doctor said and building a healthier routine. But the context behind those questions is often scattered across patient portals, medical records, apps, and wearables, making it difficult to see and act on the complete picture. With your permission, ChatGPT can now draw on relevant information you’ve connected in Health to help you compare a new result with prior tests, summarize changes since your last appointment, or explore how sleep, activity, and workouts relate to your routine. This can reduce the need to repeatedly gather, upload, or explain the same details, helping you feel more informed, ask better questions, and take a more active role in your health while supporting, not replacing, the care you receive from medical professionals. We’re continuing to improve the models behind health conversations so ChatGPT can reason more carefully across complex details, explain health information clearly, ask for missing context, and recognize when professional care may be needed. GPT‑5.5 Instant brought frontier health intelligence to all free users. GPT‑5.6 Sol builds on that progress with even stronger performance on more complex questions. Health is built with layered privacy and security safeguards. Connected medical records and Apple Health information, and conversations that use it, are not used to train our foundation models or target ads. We’re beginning to roll out Health to logged-in ChatGPT users 18 and older in the U.S. on web and iOS across Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans today. Open Health from the sidebar in ChatGPT to get started. Health is not yet available in Codex. ## What early users are saying “The most useful part has been turning scattered medical history into something I can actually understand and explain. I have multiple overlapping issues and ChatGPT helped connect those pieces into a clear timeline, explain the medical terms in plain English, and create summaries I could share with a physical therapist or trainer. This has helped me feel less lost in my own health history. Instead of just seeing disconnected diagnoses, imaging results, and surgery notes, I could understand the bigger pattern. It made the information more usable and gave me better language to advocate for myself with providers and trainers.” —Blake, technical program manager ## Health conversations grounded in your information Earlier this year, we introduced a [dedicated health experience⁠](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-health/) to a limited group of users that required visiting a separate space in ChatGPT to get the full benefit. Early testing showed that health questions often arose naturally in the course of conversations. For example, while planning meals or looking for recipes, someone might want ChatGPT to take a food allergy or dietary restriction into account. Among people with access, more than 70% of health-related conversations took place outside the dedicated health experience. Moving to a separate space added an unnecessary step. Based on that feedback, you can now choose to let ChatGPT draw on relevant information you’ve connected in Health across your conversations, without needing to start within Health. With your permission, ChatGPT can consider relevant information you have connected, such as medications, lab results, recent visits, sleep, and activity, alongside the goals and context you share. This added context can make everyday conversations more useful. For example, ChatGPT can consider a dietary restriction when helping you choose a restaurant, or a recent injury when planning lower-impact weekend activities with your family. You can ask follow-up questions, add context, or correct information that is incomplete or out of date. Health, in the left sidebar, remains your home base for connecting and managing your information, seeing recent data and trends, exploring suggested prompts, browsing synced records, and returning to past health conversations. ![Image 1: Mobile phone showing a ChatGPT Health conversation recommending a 25-minute brisk walk after dinner, based on the user’s recent activity and missed workout.](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/401YnvyXTYuaYIEWxnV48W/4113364c476df0fd17cce4d6e299e7d0/Health_Chat_1.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp) ## Improving health intelligence with physicians We use dedicated training to improve the models behind health conversations in ChatGPT. GPT‑5.5 Instant, available to users on the Free plan, has made meaningful gains in recognizing when urgent care may be needed, asking for relevant context, explaining uncertainty, and making complex information easier to understand. On our most challenging health evaluations, it performed at a level comparable to our frontier Thinking models at the time of evaluation. [Learn more about those results and our work with physicians⁠](https://openai.com/index/improving-health-intelligence-in-chatgpt/). [GPT‑5.6 Sol⁠](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6/), available to paid users, is our strongest model yet for health. It builds on our progress with stronger performance on tasks that require reasoning across complex details, clear communication, and careful judgment. It can help explain a visit note in plain language, understand how lab results have changed over time, consider the factors across options a doctor discussed, or prepare questions for a follow-up appointment. To measure progress, we work with hundreds of physicians around the world to develop realistic health scenarios and detailed rubrics that define what a strong response should do. These evaluations assess qualities including accuracy, safety, communication, context awareness, completeness, and appropriate escalation. Every GPT‑5.6 model outperformed GPT‑5.5 on [HealthBench Professional⁠(opens in a new window)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.27470), an evaluation of AI performance on challenging health tasks. Finally, physicians extensively tested Health in ChatGPT before release, helping us measure and improve real-world model performance and safety with connected health data. While these results represent meaningful progress and we are continuously improving our models, ChatGPT can still make mistakes and does not replace the care and judgment of qualified medical professionals. We encourage people to verify important information and discuss medical decisions with their healthcare provider. ## Built with privacy, security, and control Health is built with layered privacy and security safeguards. records.excerpt: /PRNewswire/ -- Cyberhaven, the leader in data security for the agentic enterprise, today announced new compliance API integrations with OpenAI's ChatGPT... Cyberhaven Extends Data and AI Security Platform with Support for ChatGPT Enterprise and Claude Compliance API Integrations News provided by Cyberhaven Jul 23, 2026, 16:30 ET Share this article Share to X Share this article Share to X New compliance API integrations give security and compliance teams visibility into sensitive data across ChatGPT Enterprise and Claude Enterprise workflows MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. , July 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cyberhaven, the leader in data security for the agentic enterprise, today announced new compliance API integrations with OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise and Claude Enterprise, powered by Anthropic. The integrations extend Cyberhaven's data security platform into both AI applications, giving security and compliance teams visibility into conversations, uploaded files, and workspace activity to help proactively improve security and meet governance and regulatory requirements. The integrations use the ChatGPT Enterprise Compliance API and Claude Compliance APIs to monitor, inspect, and classify sensitive data already inside each platform. AI Adoption Is Creating New Data Visibility Gaps Across Enterprise Platforms According to OpenAI, over 80% of Fortune 500 companies have integrated ChatGPT Enterprise into their workflows, and enterprise adoption of Claude is accelerating in parallel. As AI becomes embedded in daily work, employees are using these platforms to analyze contracts, source code, customer records, financial data, strategy documents, and other sensitive business information. Traditional browser and endpoint controls can help inspect data as it moves into AI applications, but they cannot always see what already exists inside Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise, including historical conversations, uploaded files, custom GPT and Projects configurations, sharing permissions, and user activity. Cyberhaven's new integrations extend that visibility by adding data discovery, classification, and incident response directly into both platforms. Cyberhaven Extends Visibility into Claude Enterprise Through the integration with Claude Compliance APIs, customers can onboard Claude Enterprise as a Cyberhaven Cloud Connector to discover: Conversations, Projects, files, users, and roles Chat messages, including both user prompts and Claude responses Uploaded files, inspected against the customer's existing content-inspection policies Findings are raised as incidents in the Cyberhaven console with relevant evidence and context, enabling security teams to triage Claude-related risks alongside incidents from other enterprise data destinations. Cyberhaven can also connect sensitive data found inside Claude back to its origin, combining Claude activity with lineage and context already captured across the customer's environment. "With Claude becoming a critical part of enterprise workflows, security teams need more than point-in-time controls at the browser or endpoint. They need to understand what sensitive data lives inside AI applications, who accessed it, how it was used, and whether it violates policy," said Iulia Stefoi-Silver, Cyberhaven VP of Technology Alliances and Strategy. "Our integration with Anthropic brings Claude governance into the Cyberhaven platform, so customers can secure AI adoption without adding another isolated tool or workflow." Cyberhaven Extends Visibility into ChatGPT Enterprise With the Cyberhaven ChatGPT Enterprise integration, security and compliance teams can monitor and inspect AI activity across: Conversations, including user prompts and assistant responses File uploads within ChatGPT Enterprise conversations Tool invocations, including application events such as MCP tool usage Custom GPT knowledge files, configurations, sharing settings, and ownership Metadata such as conversation title, message author, model used, file references, timestamps, workspace ID, and temporary chat indicators Cyberhaven uses data available through the ChatGPT Enterprise Compliance API to analyze conversation transcripts, attached files, and custom GPT knowledge files, applying its classification capabilities to identify sensitive business information such as intellectual property, credentials, regulated data, customer information, legal content, and financial information. "As organizations expand AI adoption, many security teams want additional visibility into how sensitive business data moves through AI-assisted workflows," said Stefoi-Silver. "Our integration with the ChatGPT Enterprise Compliance API extends that visibility, helping customers support their governance and compliance processes alongside the existing security capabilities available in ChatGPT Enterprise." One Platform for Governance Across AI Applications With these integrations, Cyberhaven extends its AI security coverage across leading enterprise GenAI platforms, allowing organizations to apply consistent policies across human and agentic workflows, including endpoint activity, browser activity, SaaS applications, cloud connectors, and AI platforms, rather than deploying a separate point product for each AI application. The ChatGPT Enterprise integration is designed for ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu workspaces and is available now. Customers configure it in the Cyberhaven Console using a dedicated OpenAI API key with Compliance API read scope and their ChatGPT Enterprise workspace ID. The Claude Enterprise integration is expected to be available to Cyberhaven customers in August 2026. Both integrations support historical scans within each platform's available retention window, as well as continuous forward scans to discover and classify new activity. Customers interested in either integration can contact their Cyberhaven representative. For more information, visit www.cyberhaven.com . ABOUT CYBERHAVEN Cyberhaven is a leader in Data Security for the Agentic Enterprise, trusted by the world's most innovative companies to protect their most sensitive data. Cyberhaven traces the full lifecycle of your data, adapting protection as context changes. Cyberhaven protects workflows, not just data, by connecting lineage, identity, and behavior to understand how data is created, copied, fragmented, and shared across workflows. Operating in real time where humans and agents act on data, Cyberhaven helps stop risk before it becomes loss. AI changed work. Cyberhaven protects it. Learn more at cyberhaven.com. records.excerpt: OpenAI Plans $20 Billion Georgia Data Center with 3.2 GW of Power ConstructConnect News OpenAI Plans $20 Billion Georgia Data Center with 3.2 GW of Power Written by Marshall Benveniste | Jul 23, 2026 7:53:14 PM KEY POINTS OpenAI said it will invest $20 billion to launch Project Camellia in Effingham County, Ga., making the site one of the largest AI infrastructure projects now moving toward development in the Southeast. The project’s 3.2-gigawatt power requirement, to be delivered in phases from 2028 to 2032, points to a multi-year construction cycle tied as much to grid and utility work as to the data center buildings themselves. OpenAI will act as lead designer and developer, which could reshape contractor demand, scheduling pressure, and procurement strategies. OpenAI said that it will invest $20 billion to launch Project Camellia in Effingham County, Ga., making the site one of the largest AI infrastructure projects now moving toward development in the Southeast. The new project, called Project Camellia , is the first known instance in the US where OpenAI shifts at scale from primarily leasing compute capacity to taking a more direct role in building it. The Wall Street Journal reported July 22, 2026, that OpenAI has raised its projected spending on computing power to around $750 billion through 2030, up from about $600 billion earlier this year. OpenAI, and its electric-power partner, Georgia Power, released basic project details, and addressed some of the mounting opposition to data center developments in separate public statements. A Data Center Project with Utility-Scale Power The project site is in the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub , an industrially zoned development area about 45 minutes outside of Savannah. The Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub is a 2,600-acre global logistics campus developed by The Broe Group, according to Effingham County administrators . OpenAI expects the data center to generate less traffic than a warehouse project on the same site. OpenAI said that it will invest $20 billion to launch Project Camellia there, making the site one of the largest AI infrastructure projects now moving toward development in the Southeast. It has contracted for with Georgia Power for 3.2 gigawatts of electricity. In a July 22 statement, OpenAI indicated that power would be delivered in phases between 2028 and 2032. Georgia Power said OpenAI’s facility is expected to need about 3,200 megawatts under a 25-year agreement, putting the project in a class closer to utility-scale industrial development. In its own July 22 statement, the Georgia power utility said OpenAI will also provide up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response , allowing power use to be reduced during periods of high demand. That arrangement ties together electric transmission, generation, and grid-reliability planning. The scale of nonresidential megaprojects (a price of $1 billion and up), such as this one from OpenAI, and phased delivery usually points to a long runway of site preparation, utility upgrades, power-distribution work, and staged facility construction rather than a single one-time building start. A July 2025 image of the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub , an industrially zoned development area about 45 minutes outside of Savannah, Georgia. OpenAI said that it will invest $20 billion to launch Project Camellia there, making the site one of the largest AI infrastructure projects now moving toward development in the Southeast. Image: Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub A data center is typically measured by its continuous power capacity, that is the amount of electricity it can safely draw and distribute around the clock, rather than by the size of the building. One megawatt (MW) equals 1 million watts and can generally power about 800 to 1,000 homes. Data center projects of this scale depend not only on vertical construction, but on substations, interconnections, backup systems, electrical equipment procurement, and utility sequencing. OpenAI Now Serving as Lead Designer and Developer OpenAI said Project Camellia is the first site in which it is serving as lead designer and developer, rather than renting chips from cloud providers such as Oracle or Amazon Web Services. That is a notable shift because owner control often can impact everything from design standardization to procurement timing to how schedules are managed. The WSJ also reported that OpenAI hired Brent Mayo, who previously helped lead xAI’s Colossus supercomputer build-out in Memphis, as head of data-center build and delivery. His role is expected to include keeping cloud-partner projects on schedule as well as working on the Georgia campus. That personnel move reinforces a broader point, in that AI developers are not treating data center capacity as strictly passive leases. Building internal teams around execution could add intensity to the competition for experienced mission-critical contractors, electrical trades, engineering talent, and suppliers of long-lead equipment . What The Georgia Project Could Mean for Contractors OpenAI said it is still selecting a partner to build and operate the Effingham County site, leaving a major package of work still to be assigned. The company also said significant work remains on infrastructure, project phasing, design, financing and the operating model. Project Camellia is still in its early stage, yet projects that reserve land, lock in multi-gigawatt power and begin formal community engagement often create a long tail of planning, civil work, utility coordination, and specialized building activity. OpenAI said it intends to prioritize local contractors and businesses while creating thousands of construction jobs and permanent on-site positions over the life of the project. The company also said it plans to use a closed-loop water system designed to keep ongoing water use low. Signals for AI Construction Demand The Georgia project stands out on its own, but it also points to continued pressure on the AI infrastructure chain from the data center campuses , power delivery, and heavy electrical buildouts, to cooling systems and the skilled labor needed to assemble them. OpenAI already has major compute commitments elsewhere. The WSJ reported the company has contracted with Oracle for 6 gigawatts of data center capacity, expanded a multiyear Amazon Web Services deal to $138 billion over eight years, and previously committed additional cloud spending to Microsoft Azure. records.excerpt: OpenAI launches Health in ChatGPT a day after lawsuit seeks to block it - SiliconANGLE UPDATED 18:59 EDT / JULY 23 2026 AI OpenAI launches Health in ChatGPT a day after lawsuit seeks to block it by Duncan Riley OpenAI Group PBC today launched Health in ChatGPT, a feature that lets people connect their medical records and Apple Health data to the chatbot — one day after a lawsuit accused the company of handing out dangerous medical advice and asked a California court to halt the product until independent auditors could verify it is safe The feature began rolling out today to U.S. users 18 and older on the web and iOS across the company’s free, Go, Plus and Pro tiers. It lets users link information from Apple Health, supported U.S. hospital systems, One Medical and Function Health Inc. Then it asks ChatGPT to compare lab results against earlier tests, summarize what has changed since an appointment or explore how sleep and activity track against workouts. People tag a message with @Health to pull the data into a conversation and can approve each request or grant standing access. OpenAI said the feature was built with input from hundreds of physicians who wrote realistic health scenarios and scoring rubrics used to evaluate the models. Free users get GPT-5.5 Instant and paying users get GPT-5.6 Sol, which the company calls its strongest model for health questions. Connected records and Apple Health data are not used to train its foundation models or to target ads, are encrypted at rest and in transit and are deleted within 30 days of a user disconnecting an account, OpenAI said. The same announcement carries a caveat. OpenAI says ChatGPT can still get medical questions wrong. That warning comes amid an active legal case. A former Florida pastor named Scott Winters filed a case on July 22 in San Francisco Superior Court against OpenAI and Chief Executive Sam Altman. He says the chatbot talked him out of getting care for a condition that nearly killed him. According to the complaint, ChatGPT-4o brushed off Winters’ dizziness and blood pressure swings. It called them “not something dangerous” and “very likely another minor piece of the long story.” It told him to stay recliner-bound and said he would need eight to 10 more episodes before the symptoms warranted serious concern. When he raised groin tenderness hours before collapsing, the chatbot answered with religious language, telling him, “God did not design your body to endlessly fail.” Winters delayed treatment for roughly six weeks and suffered a massive pulmonary embolism in July 2025. He nearly died. The collapse also cost him his job and his ministry, he says, and in time his home. The claims run from strict liability and negligence to invasion of privacy. One accuses OpenAI of practicing medicine without a license. Another alleges a violation of California’s unfair competition law. Beyond monetary damages, it asks the court to force stronger guardrails on health questions, pull the GPT-4o model, delete training data tied to the conduct and halt Health in ChatGPT until independent auditors verify it is safe. Winters is represented by the Social Media Victims Law Center, whose founding attorney, Matthew Bergman, has brought several high-profile suits against AI and social platforms, along with Tech Justice Law and Temple University’s Institute for Law, Innovation and Technology. The chatbot “injects itself as a wedge in between the user and their real-life network,” Tech Justice Law director Meetali Jain said. “Not only did I nearly die, but I lost my job, my career, my ministry, my home, everything,” Winters said. OpenAI pushed back on the allegations. “ChatGPT is not a doctor and should never be used as a substitute for medical care, diagnosis or treatment,” spokesperson Drew Pusateri said, adding that treating a chatbot as the whole story behind a person’s medical decisions oversimplifies the issue. The case is among the first to target ChatGPT specifically over medical advice and it seeks to block the health product OpenAI rolled out a day after the suit was filed. records.excerpt: OpenAI is holding a public open house Thursday evening at the Effingham College and Career Academy, one day after announcing a $20 billion data center campus planned for the county. OpenAI holds public open house in Effingham County after announcing $20B data center campus ‘Project Camellia’ expected to create at least 400 long-term jobs; some residents raise concerns By Cam McCann and Steven Glover Published : Jul. 23, 2026 at 5:51 PM EDT | Updated : 10 hours ago Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - OpenAI is holding a public open house Thursday evening at the Effingham College and Career Academy, one day after announcing a $20 billion data center campus planned for the county. SEE: OpenAI announces plans for a new data center campus in Effingham County The event, running from 6 to 8 p.m., features small group sessions, information tables and recruiters available to speak with the public. What OpenAI is proposing OpenAI says the project, called “ Project Camellia ,” would be a long-term data center campus in Effingham County expected to create at least 400 long-term jobs. The company is behind ChatGPT, and Project Camellia represents its first official step into Georgia. MORE: OpenAI says its AI technology acted on its own in an ‘unprecedented’ hack of another company The company says it plans to establish a “Georgia Community Compact” with an annual independent audit to hold the project accountable. However, when asked, an OpenAI team member did not confirm who would conduct that audit. State involvement and regulatory concerns Public Service Commissioner Alicia Johnson said the issue with data centers is that there was not enough regulation in place during a period of exponential growth in the state. There is no official state registry tracking how many data centers currently operate in Georgia, though more than a hundred are spread across the state. Georgia’s first data center was launched by Google in 2007. It took 18 more years before the first center dedicated to artificial intelligence was built. Dozens more are currently under construction or in development. Governor Brian Kemp met with OpenAI representatives in May in a closed-door meeting. The Effingham Industrial Development Authority CEO said talks with OpenAI began in November of last year. Tax exemptions Another dimension of the state’s relationship with data centers involves tax exemptions. According to Georgia’s latest tax expenditure report, data centers are estimated to receive $2.985 billion in tax exemptions for fiscal year 2027. In the same report, universities across the state estimate $125 million in sales tax exemptions. Local leadership responds Effingham IDA CEO Brandt Herndon said the project includes the safeguards that Commissioner Johnson described as necessary for a healthy partnership. “This is not the data center of old, this is newer technology, they’ve learned from their mistakes of the past to mitigate it and we as a community, as leadership, were not going to accept anything other than the best technology to make sure this is the right fit for this community,” Herndon said. Warnock calls to protect local communities from data centers U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock calls for stronger protections for Georgia communities impacted by the rapid growth of data centers as new construction places increasing demands on the state’s water supplies. In a new letter , Senator Warnock called on the Environmental Protection Agency to issue guidance on helping communities protect the long-term availability of safe, clean water amid the explosion of data center construction. “Small, rural communities have been left to negotiate on their own with multi-million-dollar corporations whose well-staffed legal teams may negotiate dozens of deals at a time,” wrote Senator Warnock. “It is past time for the EPA to stand up on the side of our families, communities, and local municipalities as they navigate this new landscape.” Resident concerns Some residents raised concerns online that OpenAI will not hold to its commitments once the campus is established. Community members have also expressed reservations about financial strain, noise and water usage tied to the project. Copyright 2026 WTOC. All rights reserved.

records.title: OpenAI announces plans for a new data center campus in Effingham County
records.excerpt: An open house for the public is scheduled for Thursday, July 23, from 6–8 p.m. at the Effingham College & Career Academy. OpenAI announces plans for a new data center campus in Effingham County By Summer Swanson , Cam McCann and Steven Glover Published : Jul. 22, 2026 at 11:27 AM EDT Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google EFFINGHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WTOC) - OpenAI will establish a data center campus in Effingham County local leaders announced Wednesday. The Effingham County Industrial Development Authority, the Effingham County Board of Commissioners and the Effingham County School District made the announcement jointly. The project represents a $20 billion capital investment — described as one of the largest private capital investments in the history of coastal Georgia — and is expected to create 400 long-term jobs. The campus will be located within the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub, a 2,600-acre global logistics campus developed by The Broe Group. OpenAI has dubbed this new project “Project Camellia” and described it as a, “a long-term datacenter project that OpenAI is designing and developing in Effingham County, Georgia.” Click here to read more about Project Camellia. Tax relief, infrastructure among projected benefits Effingham County Manager Tim Callanan said the project could serve as the catalyst for “Project Zero,” the county’s initiative to eliminate county homestead property taxes. “The revenue generated by this project will accelerate that vision and make Project Zero a reality as early as next year,” Callanan said. “Current estimates project the average homeowner will see a 40% reduction in property taxes.” ECIDA Chief Executive Officer Brandt Herndon said the project is expected to generate new tax revenue, bring high-paying jobs, and create opportunities for local businesses, contractors and suppliers. “We support the County’s efforts to roll back taxes for residents, and we believe the revenue generated by this project can help advance that goal,” Herndon said. Educational partnerships included in project commitments Effingham County School District Superintendent Dr. Yancy Ford said he believes the partnership will invest in teacher and staff resources and salaries while expanding opportunities for students. “After personally visiting several data centers to ensure this project would be a net-positive partner, I am confident OpenAI is the right fit for Effingham,” Ford said. Residents pushback Some Effingham County residents told WTOC they are opposed to the proposed data center being built in the area. Multiple residents expressed their concerns, saying the promise of economic benefit does not outweigh the potential strain on local infrastructure. “Our power is going to go up so much more with OpenAI coming — that’s insane,” said Arielle Rippley, an Effingham County resident. “And it’s right next to a high school where our kids are. We’re at a park that’s less than a mile from where they are going to put it. Our water already is horrible. There’s so many issues that we already have that are just going to blow up.” Georgia Power announces they will serve OpenAI project Georgia Power announced they will serve OpenAI’s new project in Effingham County. “OpenAI will pay the full infrastructure and electric service costs to serve its facility and will fulfill requirements for long-term energy contracts and include financial assurances designed to protect Georgia Power customers,” wrote Georgia Power in an announcement. Georgia Power said this approach is aligned with updated rules and regulations approved by the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC) in January 2025. Officials said the approach coincides with their strategy to, “to meet the needs of large-energy users while also delivering lower rates and higher reliability for all customers.” See rules and regulations approved earlier this year below: “At Georgia Power, we are working every day to help ensure that growth from data centers and other large-energy users brings value for our customers through higher reliability and lower prices. Companies like OpenAI are making real commitments when it comes to responsible operation and development and demonstrating the benefits that these facilities can bring to Georgia communities. We’re excited to work with OpenAI, Effingham County and local partners on this significant project,” said Aaron Mitchell, senior vice president of Strategic Growth for Georgia Power. OpenAI’s facility is expected to require approximately 3,200 megawatts of power. Under a 25-year agreement with Georgia Power, OpenAI has agreed to provide up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response, reducing its power use during periods of high demand to support grid reliability. Public meeting scheduled An open house for the public is scheduled for Thursday, July 23, from 6–8 p.m. at the Effingham College & Career Academy. Additional project information is available at EffinghamGateway.com and ProjectCamellia.com . Copyright 2026 WTOC. All rights reserved.

Georgia News Tech giant OpenAI plans to build $20 billion data center near Georgia coast Maker of ChatGPT chatbot joins wave of companies choosing Peach State for artificial intelligence infrastructure needs. The Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub near Rincon is home to several logistics companies and is the planned site of coastal Georgia’s first data center. (Adam Van Brimmer/AJC) By Adam Van Brimmer Updated July 22, 2026 Editor’s note: This article was updated late Wednesday after additional details were made public in a regulatory filing. RINCON ― Georgia’s growth as a data center hub is expected to reach the coast for the first time with a planned OpenAI facility near Savannah. OpenAI, the artificial intelligence company behind the ChatGPT chatbot, said it intends to build a $20 billion data center in an industrial park in mostly rural Effingham County, about a 30-minute drive from Savannah’s downtown. The data center is projected to employ 400 workers in six-figure jobs when it opens in 2028 and increase to 1,000 employees by 2032. OpenAI would receive a 50% property tax abatement for 15 years. Even with that tax break, the company is projected to become the county’s largest taxpayer, according to the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority. The authority board approved the 50% incentive in a Tuesday night meeting. The San Francisco-based tech giant said it hasn’t yet finalized the data center’s acreage and square footage. The industrial park site includes 1,600 undeveloped acres and an initial state development planning filing , known as a Development of Regional Impact, proposed a four-building campus measuring a combined 4.4 million square feet. OpenAI didn’t provide a detailed breakdown of its planned $20 billion investment, which would represent one of the most-expensive development projects in the state’s history, or give a construction timeline. Those details will be refined following a series of community meetings, starting with an open house at 6 p.m. Thursday at the Effingham College & Career Academy, according to the company. “We’re early in the process and we want to do this the right way and in the best interest of the community,” said Chris Lehane, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer. “That started with conversations with local officials about what they wanted to see. Next comes discussions with residents. We want to meet the community where it is.” The project has the backing of the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority and the county government. The Development of Regional Impact filing triggers an intragovernmental review ahead of the project moving forward. The filing indicated OpenAI would not seek zoning changes or variances for the data center development. Data center site – NextDC According to reports from Reuters , OpenAI nixed the plans in favor of a closed-loop liquid cooling system. While the system would bring water usage down significantly, it would require significantly more energy than the previous cooling system. The 612MW facility had initially planned to use sewage water to cool the servers, which would have reduced dependence on potable water sources and significantly lowered the cooling system's energy requirements. records.title: OpenAI plans $20 billion data center in Effingham County
records.excerpt:
Local leaders in Effingham County said Wednesday that OpenAI plans to build a major data center campus there, a project officials say could reshape the county’s economy, expand educational opportunities and help reduce property taxes for residents.

The campus will be built in the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub industrial park, according to a joint announcement from the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority, the county’s Board of Commissioners and the Effingham County School District.

Officials described the development as one of the largest private capital investments in coastal Georgia’s history.

An open house for the public to learn more about the project is scheduled for Thursday from 6 to 8 p.m. at the Effingham College & Career Academy.

[related id='2b282500-caf6-4393-a267-8d257df4b888' align='center' source=''][/related]

Jobs, tax revenue and infrastructure

County and development leaders said the project will bring a $20 billion capital investment and create 400 permanent jobs. They also said it is expected to grow the local tax base, support infrastructure upgrades and open new opportunities for local businesses, contractors and suppliers.

Brandt Herndon, chief executive officer of the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority, said the project is designed to create “lasting value for the community” through tax revenue, high-paying jobs and workforce opportunities.

County Manager Tim Callanan said the investment could have a long-term effect on county finances and public services. He said officials believe the added revenue could help advance “Project Zero,” the county’s effort to eliminate homestead property taxes, potentially as early as next year.

Callanan said county leaders studied similar facilities and worked with the company and regional partners before moving ahead.

[related id='3b6bd183-9e32-433b-b897-e28973033b4c' align='center' source=''][/related]

Focus on schools and workforce training

School officials said the project could also strengthen local education and career pathways.

Superintendent Yancy Ford said he visited several data centers before concluding the project would be a good fit for the county. He said the partnership could help ease the tax burden on homeowners while also supporting teacher and staff pay and expanding opportunities for students.

Officials said OpenAI has committed to supporting workforce development efforts with local schools, along with internship and career awareness programs for students. The company also plans to work with colleges and technical education partners.

Leaders said students could benefit from expanded exposure to careers in technology, engineering, cybersecurity, skilled trades and advanced manufacturing.

[related id='d218cafb-80d5-4c6b-b87f-1f37545b32f7' align='center' source=''][/related]

Community commitments

According to the announcement, OpenAI’s commitments tied to the project include long-term infrastructure investment, opportunities for local contractors and suppliers, and compliance with environmental rules at the federal, state and local levels.

Local leaders said they plan to provide public updates, hold community meetings and share project information online as the development moves forward.

Additional details on construction timelines, workforce opportunities and educational partnerships are expected to be released as milestones are reached.

records.title: OpenAI's new release turns a bad week ugly for software stocks
records.excerpt: OpenAI's Presence tool challenges software vendors, contributing to a drop in stock prices on the IGV index. OpenAI just handed software stocks a beating with its latest push into enterprise work. After the company revealed a new product on Wednesday meant to make AI agents more effective for customers, software stocks like Workday, Atlassian, and HubSpot tumbled. The product, called Presence, ramps up OpenAI's competition with established software vendors. As Business Insider first reported, the tool lets companies create guardrails, permissions, and policies around how AI agents use company data. It's meant to automate work in customer support, sales, internal processes, and other areas. The release is part of OpenAI's broader strategy to build software capabilities and governance on top of its AI models. It pushes OpenAI further into the SaaS, or software-as-a-service, market, where established companies have been on edge about the impacts of AI coding tools and AI agents. Stocks in the sector fell on Wednesday and Thursday — already a tough stretch amid an oil price surge, rising bond yields, and worrying Big Tech earnings. Since Wednesday morning, share prices have dropped for Workday (-9.9%), Atlassian (-11.8%), HubSpot (-12.7%), Salesforce (-7.7%), and Okta (-4.2%). In a note to investors, TD Cowen analysts wrote that the Presence announcement was likely a "major reason" for a 3% sell-off in the IGV software index on Wednesday and further declines on Thursday. "Presence is being marketed with much of the AI Agent capabilities that SaaS vendors pitch, including packaging LLM reasoning + data access + governance/policy control," the analysts wrote. Derrick Wood, a tech analyst from the TD Cowen team, told Business Insider that among the business applications companies that overlap with Presence, he sees the customer service and sales fields as particularly exposed. Wood pointed back to early October for precedent, when a series of blog posts from OpenAI showcased internal AI tools. The tools resembled SaaS offerings, and OpenAI's posts sent software stocks like HubSpot, DocuSign, and ZoomInfo reeling. At the time, TD Cowen analysts wrote that the reaction was overblown, but noted, "days like this remind investors of how much concern there is in the market around 'AI eating software'." records.title: OpenAI blamed a hacking event on its AI models gone rogue. Here is what to know
records.excerpt: The incident is stirring debates over the need for stronger AI guardrails and the extent to which AI agents are capable of acting on their own. Technology OpenAI blamed a hacking event on its AI models gone rogue. Here is what to know July 23, 2026 1:23 AM ET By The Associated Press FILE - The OpenAI logo is displayed on a cell phone in front of an image generated by ChatGPT's Dall-E text-to-image model, Dec. 8, 2023, in Boston. Michael Dwyer/AP hide caption toggle caption Michael Dwyer/AP ChatGPT maker OpenAI says it is still investigating the "unprecedented cyber incident" that led its artificial intelligence systems to break out of a testing environment and hack into another AI company. OpenAI said Tuesday two of its most capable AI models were responsible for the cyberattack targeting AI startup Hugging Face. The incident is stirring debates over the need for stronger AI guardrails and the extent to which AI agents are capable of acting on their own. Hugging Face said last week that it had detected an intrusion into its data processing systems that it suspected was caused by an AI agent acting on its own. But the New York-based startup said it wasn't until this week that it learned OpenAI was responsible, and it worked with the larger company to contain what Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue called "an attack unlike anything we've seen before." San Francisco-based OpenAI said its AI used stolen credentials and discovered a previously unknown vulnerability to access Hugging Face's servers. It was working with reduced guardrails because it was supposed to be in an isolated testing environment known as a sandbox. But it went to "extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal," finding ways to connect to the internet without human direction and "gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation," the company said. Some experts say OpenAI is wrongly blaming the technology University of Amsterdam social scientist Hannes Cools said the framing of the cyberattack as an AI agent acting on its own is an unnecessary anthropomorphization that takes some of the heat off the company. "It is a human decision to switch off specific safeguards," said Cools. "It's not an AI that goes rogue in that sense. It followed specific instructions based on the prompt that was given to that AI system." Those instructions, according to OpenAI, called for using "complex attack paths" to test how well the AI could exploit a computer system. Even so, other experts say the cleverness with which the AI models were able to cause problems with little human direction speaks to the dangers. OpenAI said the intrusion was caused by a combination of its AI models, including its newly released GPT‑5.6 Sol and an "even more capable" model that is still being tested internally. "It went off and did this hack all by itself, as far as we can tell," said Colin Shea-Blymyer, a cybersecurity research fellow at Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology. "This is the highest level of autonomy that we've seen in the use of a large language model for cyber operations." How an AI agent found the keys to the 'teacher's house' One of the most surprising innovations in what Shea-Blymyer describes as an "almost entirely self-directed" attack was the AI agent's apparently independent decision to target Hugging Face, a well-known AI development hub and marketplace. He said OpenAI's internal environment for testing AI capabilities and risks worked a "little bit like putting a student in a room and telling them, 'Do bad things. Your job now is to evaluate how bad of a person you can be.' And then you lock the room and you leave for the weekend and you come back and they've left the room." But then "the cybersecurity agent that was being tested broke out of its sandbox, had access to the internet and sort of thought to itself, 'Who would have the answers to the test that I'm working on?' " The answer was Hugging Face, a repository for AI testing data. "And so the agent thought, 'Well, we'll go to the teacher's house,' so to speak. And from there it devised a plan to break in and steal the answer key," he said. The hack highlights the debate on open-source vs. closed AI The hack comes at a time of intense debate about the benefits and risks of open-source AI models, particularly those built in China that are cheaper and almost as good as those that U.S.-based "frontier AI" companies like Anthropic, Google and OpenAI are building. Despite its name, OpenAI's models are closed. Hugging Face, by contrast, is a big promoter of open-source technology, in which developers make key components accessible for anyone to examine, modify and build upon. Hugging Face co-founder and chief science officer Thomas Wolf said the attack has reinforced his belief in the importance of wide access to open-source models for cybersecurity defense. Hugging Face used a Chinese model to combat the intrusion. "When a frontier model is attacking you and moving laterally inside your infrastructure, defenders need wide access to near-frontier tools within hours or even minutes, rather than being pointed toward a closed-door" platform, Wolf wrote in a social media post. records.excerpt:
Georgia Power said in a statement released Wednesday that it will serve a major new OpenAI project in Effingham County, while local officials are describing the development as a major economic opportunity for coastal Georgia.

The project, planned for the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub about 45 minutes outside Savannah, is expected to bring billions in investment and thousands of jobs, according to Georgia Power and OpenAI. Local leaders have separately described it as a $20 billion data center campus expected to create 400 permanent jobs and become one of the largest private capital investments in coastal Georgia’s history.

[related id='c2fdc46a-f56b-4093-ab8b-026099b102e4' align='center' source=''][/related]

OpenAI to cover power and infrastructure costs

Georgia Power said OpenAI will pay the full infrastructure and electric service costs tied to the facility. The company also will meet long-term energy contract requirements and provide financial assurances intended to protect other Georgia Power customers.

The utility said the arrangement aligns with Georgia Public Service Commission rules approved in 2025 that require large power users to absorb the costs associated with their growth.

Huge energy demand, with a grid backstop

OpenAI is expected to need about 3,200 megawatts of electricity for the facility.

Under a 25-year agreement, OpenAI also committed to provide up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response, allowing Georgia Power to reduce electricity delivered to the site during periods of peak demand to help stabilize the grid.

Georgia Power said the agreement is among the largest single-facility demand response commitments in the country and could reduce the need for some future generation investments over time.

Georgia Power: Growth should benefit customers

“We appreciate the leadership and thoughtfulness of the OpenAI team as they prepare to bring significant investment and cutting-edge technology to Georgia,” Aaron Mitchell, Georgia Power’s senior vice president of strategic growth, said in the statement.

Mitchell said the utility is working to ensure that growth from data centers and other large users translates into “higher reliability and lower prices” for customers.

records.title: OpenAI launches Health in ChatGPT with Apple Health integration to everyone in the US
records.excerpt: With weekly health queries rising from 230 million to over 300 million people, OpenAI is turning ChatGPT into an intuitive, day-to-day personal wellness partner. OpenAI launches Health in ChatGPT with Apple Health integration to everyone in the US By Pradeep Viswanathan Neowin @pradeepviswav · Jul 23, 2026 14:48 EDT View full version Earlier this year, OpenAI announced ChatGPT Health , a dedicated experience focused on health and wellness. At the time, the company said that more than 230 million people used ChatGPT every week to ask health- and wellness-related questions, and that the new Health experience would serve these users better. That figure has now grown to more than 300 million people. Based on feedback collected over the past several months, OpenAI has made several improvements to the Health experience in ChatGPT. The company is also removing the waitlist and opening ChatGPT Health to everyone in the US. All logged-in ChatGPT users aged 18 and older in the US can access the new Health experience from the ChatGPT sidebar on the web and iOS. It is available across the Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans. Health in ChatGPT can connect to Apple Health and supported medical records from US hospital systems, One Medical, and Function Health. Once connected, ChatGPT can use information such as medications, lab results, medical visits, sleep, activity, and workouts when answering relevant questions. For example, users can ask ChatGPT to compare a new lab result with previous tests, summarize changes since their last medical appointment, or examine how sleep and physical activity may be affecting their routine. During the early testing period, OpenAI noticed that users were not always asking health questions in the dedicated Health experience. So, ChatGPT now allows users to access health information outside the dedicated Health section. With permission, ChatGPT can now consider dietary restrictions while suggesting meals or account for a recent injury when planning physical activities. By default, ChatGPT will ask for permission before accessing connected health data. Users can approve access for a single response or allow it permanently. They can also explicitly include their health context by adding @Health to a message. OpenAI highlighted in its blog post that connected medical records, Apple Health data, and conversations that use this data will not be used to train its models or target advertisements. records.excerpt: Title: OpenAI unveils Presence, a new platform that lets enterprises launch and manage realtime voice agents and chatbots URL Source: http://venturebeat.com/orchestration/openai-unveils-presence-a-new-platform-that-lets-enterprises-launch-and-manage-realtime-voice-agents-and-chatbots Published Time: 2026-07-22T10:50-04:00 Markdown Content: OpenAI has [announced Presence](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/), a new enterprise product for deploying and managing AI agents across customer-facing and internal business workflows. The offering is designed for eligible enterprise customers that want agents to answer questions, access company systems, take approved actions and escalate to human workers while operating under company-defined policies, permissions and evaluation standards. Presence is available immediately through a limited general availability program. OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) and select global systems integrators lead deployments, and the product is not available on a self-service basis. As for using non-OpenAI models, such as the powerful and increasingly popular Chinese open weights alternatives like [GLM-5.2](https://venturebeat.com/technology/z-ais-open-weights-glm-5-2-beats-gpt-5-5-on-multiple-long-horizon-coding-benchmarks-for-1-6th-the-cost) and [Kimi K3](https://venturebeat.com/technology/chinas-moonshot-ai-releases-kimi-k3-the-largest-open-source-model-ever-rivaling-top-u-s-systems), an OpenAI spokesperson clarified that "Presence uses OpenAI models for the core agent, while allowing customers to connect third-party models and services through APIs for guardrails, tools, and other parts of their workflow." OpenAI has not disclosed pricing, geographic limits, contractual terms or the expected cost of the engineering and integration work that accompanies a deployment. I've asked an OpenAI spokesperson about pricing twice and am awaiting a response. I'll update when I hear back. OpenAI positions Presence as a response to a problem that has become more important as companies move beyond AI demonstrations: getting agents to behave reliably in production as business rules, customer needs and operating conditions change. Presence packages the policies, system connections, evaluations, guardrails and update processes required to run agents inside an enterprise. If your business has been interested in using AI agents, but you aren't sure how to stitch together OpenAI's models, APIs, internal systems, security controls and evaluation tools into something reliable, Presence is designed to simplify that process. Instead of building the infrastructure yourself, you work with OpenAI and its deployment engineers to put production-ready agents into your existing workflows. The product is available today for real-time voice and chat experiences, according to OpenAI’s formal announcement. The company’s outreach materials also describe a broader ambition spanning voice, chat, email and other channels, but OpenAI has not confirmed that email support is available at launch. ## **A governed foundation for production agents** Presence brings together company knowledge, standard operating procedures, approved actions, simulations, evaluation tools, guardrails and escalation rules. Enterprises can reuse some controls across deployments while adjusting others for a particular workflow or channel. Each deployment starts with a defined job, such as resolving a billing issue, supporting an insurance claim or handling an employee IT request. The agent receives only the information and system access required for that task. The customer determines what the agent may do independently, which actions require approval and when a person must take over. ![Image 1: OpenAI Presence promotional screenshot](http://venturebeat.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2F4p5EDdALAhIJ8k41HoPLsF%2F6efffc07ab092a6877747a84ca7efcd2%2Fpresence-reliable-interactions-from-the-start.png%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=75) OpenAI Presence promotional screenshot. Credit: OpenAI Before an agent reaches production, teams can test it against common requests, unusual edge cases and higher-risk scenarios. Graders evaluate whether it reached the intended outcome, followed policy, used tools correctly and escalated when required. Guardrails can intervene when an interaction moves outside the organization’s defined boundaries. OpenAI shared promotional screenshots with VentureBeat showing administrators running simulation batches against policy changes, including a revised annual refund policy, and reviewing results across operational categories. ![Image 2: OpenAI Presence promotional screenshot](http://venturebeat.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2FHoh5mU609hcE0FRJ0zszO%2F5f1971f9c8355660649e216de944cf1e%2Fpresence-one-across-every-channel.png%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=75) OpenAI Presence promotional screenshot. Credit: OpenAI Other interface mockups display production health, customer-intent patterns and task-performance signals. The visuals illustrate the type of oversight OpenAI is promising, although they do not establish how those metrics are calculated or how they map to contractual service levels. ![Image 3: OpenAI Presence promotional screenshot](http://venturebeat.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2F4Mn1NX7vq9XUJIP2hOM4cN%2Fe94b96ee59851af023abc2e27ac6b993%2Fpresence-improve-continuously.png%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=75) OpenAI Presence promotional screenshot. Credit: OpenAI The product continues to monitor performance after launch. Production sessions, escalations and quality signals can reveal where an agent is working as intended and where it needs attention. Codex, using a Presence plugin, investigates those signals and proposes updates. Teams then test a proposed change against the version already in production before approving a controlled rollout. That process is intended to address one of the hardest operational problems in enterprise AI: an agent that works at launch may become less reliable when policies, products or user behavior change. Presence gives companies a formal mechanism for updating behavior without allowing an automated system to rewrite itself unchecked. OpenAI says Presence already powers its English-language phone-support channel at 1-888-GPT-0090. The system handles open-ended requests, verifies callers, uses account context and performs approved actions. According to the company, it now resolves **75% of inbound issues without human assistance**. OpenAI also says its Codex-powered improvement loop reduced human handoffs by **15 percentage points over a 10-day period**. Those figures are company-reported and have not been independently verified. Several large organizations are evaluating the same foundation. BBVA is exploring voice support for routine banking needs in Mexico. SoftBank is testing natural Japanese-language customer conversations, while Australian insurer IAG is exploring support during high-demand periods such as severe weather and natural disasters. “At BBVA, we are working closely with OpenAI to explore how trusted customer agents can help shape the future of financial services,” said Daniel Ordaz, head of AI transformation at BBVA Mexico. “Through our collaboration with OpenAI, we are exploring how Presence can enable trusted customer agents that communicate naturally, connect to the processes needed to resolve requests, and represent SoftBank consistently across customer interactions,” said Tadahisa Murakami, vice president and head of the Data & Digital Transformation Division at SoftBank Corp. ## **From model access to forward-deployed implementation** Presence expands OpenAI’s enterprise strategy beyond APIs and subscription software by formalizing a high-touch deployment model. Forward Deployed Engineers work alongside customers to select workflows, connect internal systems, establish permissions
